questions.q: What is a Snowflake file format object for?
options: A named, reusable set of parsing rules (delimiter, header, quoting, etc.) that COPY INTO can reference instead of repeating inline
A way to convert a table into a different storage engine
A setting that controls warehouse compute size
A required step before creating any stage
questions.explain: File format objects let you define parsing rules once and reuse them across many COPY INTO calls, rather than specifying options inline every time.

options: A delimiter character appearing inside a field's own text and incorrectly splitting it into an extra column
Duplicate rows being loaded twice
A file being loaded from the wrong stage
A warehouse suspending mid-load
questions.explain: Quoting fields (e.g. with double quotes) lets a comma inside the field's text be treated as literal content rather than a column separator.

questions.q: What happens to a JSON file containing a top-level array of objects if STRIP_OUTER_ARRAY is NOT set?
options: The whole array loads as a single row instead of one row per object
The load fails immediately with an error
Only the first object in the array loads
Each object automatically becomes its own table
questions.explain: Without STRIP_OUTER_ARRAY = TRUE, Snowflake treats the entire [ ... ] array as one VARIANT value in a single row rather than unwrapping it into multiple rows.

questions.q: Why does a Parquet file format definition often need almost no options?
options: Parquet files already carry their own schema and columnar structure, unlike CSV which needs delimiter/quoting rules spelled out
Parquet cannot be loaded into Snowflake at all
Parquet files are always converted to CSV before loading
Parquet requires a separate license to configure options
questions.explain: Because Parquet is self-describing and columnar, TYPE = 'PARQUET' is frequently the entire file format definition needed.

questions.q: In this lesson's CSV example, what does SKIP_HEADER = 1 do?
options: Skips the first row of the file, typically a column-name header row
Skips every first column in each row
Loads only the header row and discards the rest
Deletes the first table row after loading
questions.explain: SKIP_HEADER = 1 tells Snowflake to skip one header line at the top of each file before parsing data rows.
